it has no knowledge of whether that will lead to meaningful statistical changes."}]},{"claim_text":"Autovacuum may skip a table whose statistical distribution changed meaningfully if only a few rows were touched.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 1 states that scheduling is based strictly on row counts and that autovacuum has no knowledge of meaningful statistical changes, so such a change with few row changes can be missed.","citations":[{"index":1,"quote":"The daemon schedules ANALYZE strictly as a function of the number of rows inserted or updated; Thus 'never' is incorrect.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"Inheritance parents will only be analyzed if the parent itself is changed - changes to child tables do not trigger autoanalyze on the parent table."}]},{"claim_text":"Autovacuum runs ANALYZE on a partitioned table only after its partitions change significantly.","verdict":"CONTRADICTED","reasoning":"Passage 6 states that autovacuum does not issue ANALYZE commands for partitioned tables at all.","citations":[{"index":6,"quote":"The autovacuum daemon does not issue ANALYZE commands for partitioned tables."}]},{"claim_text":"A timestamp column that records each row's update time will probably need more frequent statistics updates than a column of URLs.","verdict":"SUPPORTED","reasoning":"Passage 3 gives exactly this example, saying the timestamp column will probably need more frequent updates than a URL column.","citations":[{"index":3,"quote":"a timestamp column that contains the time of row update will have a constantly-increasing maximum value as rows are added and updated; such a column will probably need more frequent statistics updates than, say, a column containing URLs for pages accessed on a website."}]}]}
